title: Choose the About page structure
question: The design system is settled; this choice is how About is arranged. The roll dealt The Index first. Lock one, steer it, or re-roll.

options.label: The Index
options.lineage: The index at the back of a technical manual
options.thesis: Lead with everything Jason works with, each skill pointing at the project that proves it, then the bio in full.
options.viewport: Title and the one-line summary across the top; the six skill groups fill three index columns from the label split, references in cobalt.
options.risk: The bio, the part peers read for, starts below the fold, and unlinked groups like Apple platforms sit visibly bare.

options.label: The Datasheet
options.thesis: The bio reads as the description, with the hard facts in a ruled table beside it and skills in a full-width table below.
options.viewport: Bio in a reading column on the left; Education, Experience, Languages and base in a ruled table on the right; the skills table starts at the fold.
options.risk: A table of skills can read like a form, and the idea turns costume if any heading borrows datasheet jargon.

options.label: The Summary Strip
options.lineage: The four six-hour quarters of the Home price chart
options.thesis: Four facts on the grid's quarter lines answer the skim, then the bio reads uninterrupted, with the skills index after it.
options.viewport: Title, then a full-width strip of four facts set between the quarter lines; the bio opens beneath it in one reading column.
options.risk: The strip repeats facts the bio also states, and four equal cells can slide toward a stat-tile row if set loosely.
